key_insight: A monolayer graphene front contact improves current collection and fill factor in AlInN/Si solar cells, boosting overall efficiency without significantly changing open-circuit voltage.
engineering_relevance: Graphene can serve as a low-temperature, semitransparent conductive contact that enhances nitride-based solar cell performance while remaining compatible with device integration on Si substrates.
method: AlxIn1-xN solar cells were grown on p-type Si(100) with a thin amorphous-Si buffer layer.
Three Al compositions were tested: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43.
A monolayer graphene film was transferred onto the front surface as a semitransparent contact and devices were compared with/without graphene under light and dark conditions.
evidence_signal: Across all three compositions, the graphene contact increased short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency, while open-circuit voltage stayed nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The benefit is shown on a limited set of compositions and relies on a transfer process, so graphene uniformity and interface quality could be key implementation risks.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
